title: Secret bindings resolve through the project's secrets contract, never plaintext in the wrangler manifest
description: Every secret the Worker reads at runtime is referenced implicitly through the runtime's env accessor (in the default JS/TS Worker, `env.<NAME>`); wrangler 4.x has no `[secrets]` block, no `secrets.required[]` list, and no empty-value binding entry for secrets, and the vendor treats every such env-accessor reference from Worker code as an implicit secret binding declaration, refusing `wrangler deploy` when a referenced secret has not been set on the target. Each such name is populated on the deploy target through the vendor's own secret-set flow (first-deploy via `wrangler deploy --secrets-file <tmp>`, steady-state via `wrangler secret put <NAME>`; see `assets/wrangler-samples/bootstrap-vs-steady-state.md`). The value is sourced from the project's secrets contract (as fixed by the `security-secrets-management` blueprint at slug `security-secrets-management` when applied, or by the equivalent project-authored contract). No secret VALUE ever lives in `wrangler.toml`, in a committed environment file, in a CI variable readable outside the promote job, or in the CI run's captured logs. A CI-side redactor scrubs any log line that would emit a resolved secret value.
rationale: Secrets in deploy config is one of the two shapes of leak this blueprint refuses (the other is production auto-promote). Declaring bindings by name only forces the value to arrive through a controlled channel and keeps the manifest safe to review in a PR. The blueprint mandates the CONTRACT (values arrive through the secrets pipeline); the vendor default binds through `wrangler secret put`.
